question: Should the denylist remain a union of `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`, or should one persisted surface become the canonical owner before this security contract merges?
rationale: Both designs can be implemented safely, but choosing the permanent policy owner determines configuration complexity, editing UX, upgrade expectations, and which host must authoritatively revalidate commands; repository policy does not allow automation to choose that contract.

options.title: Use one canonical owner
options.body: Keep the denylist in `exec-approvals.json` initially and remove the parallel `tools.exec.denylist` surface unless a concrete missing use case is established.

options.title: Approve the union model
options.body: Retain both surfaces only with explicit ownership approval and documentation of precedence, editing responsibilities, compatibility, and migration behavior.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave the linked feature issue open while maintainers redesign a narrower deny-by-exception contract with less cross-host state.

recommendation.title: Use one canonical owner
recommendation.body: Keep the denylist in `exec-approvals.json` initially and remove the parallel `tools.exec.denylist` surface unless a concrete missing use case is established.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion already identifies this person as the likely owner for the exec policy and security-boundary decision, with adjacent approval-flow history.
